prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Labour Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core message: After 14 years of Conservative “chaos,” Labour promises national renewal focused on serving working people. The plan is fiscally disciplined, partnership-led with business and communities, and organised around five missions, underpinned by national security, secure borders, and economic stability.

Five missions
- Growth: Highest sustained G7 growth; partnership industrial strategy; planning reform; devolution; New Deal for Working People; skills and apprenticeships.
- Clean energy: Zero-carbon electricity by 2030; Great British Energy (publicly owned); cut bills, create 650,000 jobs; home insulation; restore climate leadership.
- Safer communities: Halve serious violent crime; restore neighbourhood policing; tackle antisocial behaviour and shoplifting; knife crime plan; rebuild confidence in policing/justice.
- Opportunity: Childcare expansion; free primary breakfast clubs; 6,500 new teachers; modern curriculum and assessment; Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; fairer HE settlement.
- NHS fit for the future: Cut waiting times (40,000 extra weekly appointments); double CT/MRI scanners; return of the family doctor; dentistry rescue; 8,500 extra mental health staff; shift care into communities; prevention focus.

Strong foundations
- National security: Unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP; counter hostile states, cyber and extremism; Martyn’s Law.
- Secure borders: Scrap Rwanda; Border Security Command with counter-terror-style powers; EU security deal; clear backlog, end hotel use; faster returns; more caseworkers and enforcement.
- Economic stability: Fiscal rules—balance current budget; debt falling by year 5; OBR oversight; no rises to NI, Income Tax rates or VAT; tackle tax avoidance; abolish non-dom; close private equity “carried interest” loophole.

Economy and jobs
- Industrial strategy with a statutory council; sector plans (automotive, life sciences, creative, financial services).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd-in private capital (ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, green hydrogen).
- Business tax stability: Cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Infrastructure: 10-year strategy; new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform; national 5G/gigabit by 2030; rail brought into public ownership as contracts end; bus franchising powers; EV charging rollout.
- Housing: 1.5m homes; restore mandatory targets; brownfield-first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; boost social/affordable housing; first-time buyer support; leasehold abolition and commonhold default; renters’ rights—end Section 21.

Clean energy and nature
- Double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; new nuclear (Hinkley, Sizewell C, SMRs); strategic gas reserve; no new North Sea exploration (no licence revocations); tougher windfall tax.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn for 5m upgrades; PRS minimum standards by 2030.
- Water: Special measures for polluting firms; tougher fines/bonuses blocked; independent monitoring.
- Farming and animal welfare: Public sector local/higher-standard food target; ELMs that work; end badger cull; ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling, snares; phase out animal testing.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders; new offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime: mandatory interventions; bans on zombie blades, machetes; liability for non-compliant online sales; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Violence against women and girls: Halve in a decade; specialist rape units and courts; stronger stalking/spiking laws; domestic abuse experts in 999.
- Prisons/probation: Build capacity; reduce reoffending; strategic probation review; Hillsborough Law; act on infected blood, Grenfell, Covid inquiries.

Public services and equality
- Child poverty strategy; UC review; triple lock retained; homelessness strategy.
- Arts, culture and sport access; football regulator; ticket resale protections.
- Equality: Socio-economic duty; Race Equality Act; disability and ethnicity pay gap reporting; strengthened women’s rights; full, trans-inclusive ban on conversion practices; modernise gender recognition law.

Governance and foreign policy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; restrict MPs’ second jobs; Lords reform (remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80) with long-term replacement.
- Votes at 16; reset with devolved governments; Council of the Nations and Regions.
- Foreign policy: Reconnected alliances; better EU relationship (no SM/CU/FOM); security pact and trade fixes (veterinary, MRAs); support for Ukraine; AUKUS; balanced China approach; Clean Power Alliance; modern trade strategy; restore development leadership (0.7% when affordable); support two-state solution and recognise Palestinian state as part of a renewed peace process.
